answer_1.quote: Automatic chart summarization is a task where the goal is to explain a chart and summarize key takeaways from it in natural language.
answer_1.outputs: Textual descriptions summarizing key insights from charts

answer_2.quote: Measures For automatic evaluation of the summary quality, we utilized five measures. BLEU and CIDEr measure n-gram overlaps between the model generated text and the reference text. CIDEr computes TF-IDF weighted n-gram overlaps. BLEURT ) is a model-based evaluation metric that indicates to what extent the candidate is grammatical and conveys the meaning of the reference. ... Content Selection (CS) metric measures how well the generated summaries match the gold summaries in terms of selecting records to generate ... Finally, for readability and fluency, we measure Perplexity (PPL) using a pre-trained GPT-2 Medium .

answer_4.quote: To further assess the summary quality we performed a human evaluation on 150 randomly sampled charts from the Statista dataset with four internal annotators who are native speakers of English. ... They compared the summaries based on three criteria: (i) Factual correctness: Which summary is more factually correct (i.e., facts mentioned are supported by the chart)? (ii) Coherence: Which summary is more coherent (i.e., sentences are well connected)? and (iii) Fluency: Which summary is more fluent and grammatically correct?
answer_4.guideline: For each criterion, the annotator picked the better one (win) or equally good (tie).
